page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is a compute-oriented virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel processor. The instance configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core using 2 threads per core, combined with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix math, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include bundled local storage, nor does it feature GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate balanced single-threaded execution paired with throughput constraints typical of low vCPU counts. Single-core performance registers within average ranges, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1836.0 and a single-core stress-ng score of 1657.98, supported by respectable single-threaded gzip compression at 28.31 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 2242.0 reflect the physical limits of a single dual-threaded core. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 17.81 GB/sec for reads and 11.0 GB/sec for writes, which contributes to lower relative rankings on memory-intensive benchmarks, including 1006.28 operations in database testing and 2.31 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

From an efficiency standpoint, the reduced memory footprint provides a compact resource allocation profile without the overhead of unneeded RAM. This setup aligns with processing pipelines that require modern Intel CPU vector extensions without large operational memory footprints. Best-fit workloads for this instance include lightweight web serving, stateless microservices, background job workers, API gateways, and light inference tasks using small language models.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an entry-tier compute-oriented virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single Intel x86_64 physical core and 4.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it allocates 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. Synthetic benchmarks show average single-core capability, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 1836.0 and solid single-threaded compression performance. Due to its two-thread limit and modest uncached memory bandwidth of 17.81 GB/sec read, multi-core metrics and database-intensive transactions fall in lower percentiles. The instance delivers lean compute density without the overhead of surplus memory, making it practical for lightweight compute workloads, stateless microservices, basic web serving, and small background automation jobs.
og_description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 offers 2 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM. Designed without local disks or GPUs, it provides baseline compute density for lightweight microservices and web serving.

tagline: An entry-level dual-vCPU compute configuration offering dedicated processing resources with a compact memory footprint for lightweight services and stateless tasks.
bullet_points: 2 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs across 1 physical core with multithreading
4.0 GB system memory providing a compact 1:2 core-to-memory ratio
Advanced instruction support including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration
